hook: Rama walked from Ayodhya to Lanka. Plot the places that tradition links to his exile, and the route crosses most of the Indian subcontinent.

beats.narration: Rama walked from Ayodhya to Lanka. Plot the places that tradition links to his exile, and the route crosses most of the Indian subcontinent.

One thing first. Valmiki names these places. He doesn't give map coordinates. The modern sites you'll see are traditional identifications, believed by pilgrims for centuries, not archaeological proof.
beats.claim: Valmiki names many of these places but does not give modern map locations.

beats.narration: It starts in Ayodhya, capital of the kingdom of Kosala. King Dasharatha has three queens and four sons. Rama is the eldest, and the king decides to crown him.
beats.claim: Dasharatha, king of Kosala, had three wives; he decided to crown Rama.

beats.narration: But years earlier, Queen Kaikeyi had saved Dasharatha's life in battle, and he promised her two boons. A maid named Manthara convinces her to cash them in.
beats.claim: Kaikeyi received two boons after saving Dasharatha in battle; Manthara persuaded her to use them.

beats.narration: Boon one: her son Bharata gets the throne. Boon two: Rama goes into exile, in the Dandaka forest, for fourteen years.
beats.claim: Kaikeyi asked for Bharata's installation and Rama's exile to the Dandaka forest for fourteen years.

beats.narration: Rama accepts without protest. A king's word must be kept. His wife Sita and his brother Lakshmana refuse to stay behind.
beats.claim: Rama is exiled with Sita and Lakshmana for 14 years.

beats.narration: Stop two. Shringverpur, on the Ganga. Here the boatman-king Guha ferries them across the river.
beats.claim: Shringverpur on the Ganga is where Guha met Rama.

beats.narration: Then Prayagraj, where the Ganga and Yamuna meet, and the hermitage of the sage Bharadvaja.
Stop four. Chitrakoot. Their first real forest home.
beats.claim: Chitrakoot was the first forest home.

beats.narration: Back in Ayodhya, Dasharatha dies of grief. Bharata, horrified at what his mother has done, walks to Chitrakoot to bring Rama home.
beats.claim: After Rama's departure Dasharatha dies of grief; Bharata goes to bring Rama back.

beats.narration: Rama refuses. Fourteen years means fourteen years. So Bharata takes Rama's sandals, places them on the throne, and rules as a caretaker.
beats.claim: Rama refuses to return before the exile ends.

beats.narration: Then they go deep south, into Dandakaranya, a vast forest that tradition places across central India, including the Bastar region of today's Chhattisgarh.
beats.claim: Chhattisgarh's Ram Van Gaman circuit includes Jagdalpur in Bastar.

beats.narration: Stop six. Panchavati, on the Godavari, at today's Nashik. The name means five banyan trees. This is where the story turns.
beats.claim: Panchavati at Nashik on the Godavari; the name means five banyan trees.

beats.narration: Here, Ravana's sister Surpanakha meets the brothers and is spurned. Lakshmana cuts off her nose, and she flies to Lanka for revenge.
beats.claim: Surpanakha, Ravana's sister, is spurned and mutilated by Lakshmana, setting up the abduction.

beats.narration: A golden deer appears. Rama chases it. Lakshmana follows. And Ravana, king of Lanka, carries Sita away.
beats.claim: Panchavati is where Sita was carried off.

beats.narration: The old vulture Jatayu tries to stop him and falls. Tradition places that fight at Lepakshi, in today's Andhra Pradesh.
beats.claim: Lepakshi is linked with Jatayu.

beats.narration: Searching south, the brothers reach Kishkindha, the kingdom of the vanaras. It's usually identified with the area around Hampi, on the Tungabhadra river.
beats.claim: Kishkindha is often identified with the region around the Tungabhadra near Hampi.

beats.narration: Earlier, deep in the forest, an old woman named Shabari, who had waited years for Rama, had welcomed them and pointed them toward Sugriva.
beats.claim: Shabari directs Rama to Sugriva.

beats.narration: Sugriva is a monkey prince in hiding, driven out by his brother Vali. Rama kills Vali, and Sugriva becomes king. In return, he sends his search parties out in every direction.
beats.claim: Rama kills Vali and restores Sugriva, who sends search parties for Sita.

beats.narration: Sugriva's minister Hanuman crosses the sea, finds Sita in Lanka, shows her Rama's ring, and brings back her jewel as proof.
Before he leaves, Hanuman lets himself be captured. His tail is set on fire, and he uses it to burn Lanka.
beats.claim: Hanuman's tail is set on fire and he burns Lanka.

beats.narration: Ravana's own brother, Vibhishana, begs him to return Sita. Ravana throws him out, and Vibhishana crosses over to Rama's side.
beats.claim: Vibhishana, Ravana's brother, defects to Rama.

beats.narration: The army marches to the coast at Rameswaram, the last stop in India.
beats.claim: Rameswaram is where the army crossed to Lanka.

beats.narration: In the epic, the vanaras build a bridge across the sea. Today, between Rameswaram's island and Sri Lanka's Mannar Island, there's a chain of limestone shoals about forty eight kilometres long, called Ram Setu, or Adam's Bridge.
beats.claim: Adam's Bridge / Ram Setu is a 48 km chain of limestone shoals between Rameswaram (Pamban) Island and Mannar Island.

beats.narration: Geologists describe the shoals as natural, a former land link exposed and drowned as sea levels changed. For millions of devotees, it is Rama's bridge. You can hold both facts at once.
beats.claim: Adam's Bridge is described as natural limestone shoals; geological evidence suggests a former land connection.

beats.narration: The war is fought in Lanka. Ravana falls. Sita is free. And fourteen years after they left, they fly home to Ayodhya.
Add up only the straight lines between these stops, and it's already about three and a half thousand kilometres. On foot, through forest, it would be far more.
beats.claim: Great-circle sum of Ayodhya→Shringverpur→Prayagraj→Chitrakoot→Jagdalpur→Nashik→Lepakshi→Hampi→Rameswaram ≈ 3,583 km.

beats.narration: Today, governments are turning this into a pilgrimage circuit, the Ram Van Gaman Path. Two hundred and forty eight places in India and Sri Lanka have been identified along it.
beats.claim: A total of 248 places in India and Sri Lanka have been identified on the Ram Van Gaman Path.

beats.narration: So that's the journey. Nine stops, one promise, fourteen years. Which of these places would you visit first? Tell me in the comments.

title: Rama’s 14-Year Exile in Shadow Puppets | Ayodhya to Lanka on a Map
description: Ayodhya, Chitrakoot, Panchavati, Kishkindha, Rameswaram: the places tradition links to Rama's exile, plotted in order. Version followed: Valmiki Ramayana. Modern sites are traditional identifications; Valmiki gives no map coordinates.
